subsystems.name: Edge devices
subsystems.role: the machines producing data where it is created — cameras, vehicle computers, factory controllers, phones.

subsystems.name: Edge node
subsystems.role: a small server enclosure doing the computation near the devices, often one or a few racks.

subsystems.name: Connectivity and local breakout
subsystems.role: carries traffic between devices, the edge node and the central cloud.
parts: local traffic breakout so data need not travel to a distant core

subsystems.name: Runtime and application stack
subsystems.role: the software that actually runs workloads on constrained hardware.

subsystems.name: Orchestration and fleet management
subsystems.role: lets one team operate thousands of unattended sites reliably.

subsystems.name: Security and identity
subsystems.role: edge sites sit in physically reachable places, so trust must be hardware-anchored.

buildSteps.title: Decide what must be local
buildSteps.detail: Work out which processing genuinely needs low latency, high bandwidth, offline operation or data-residency — and leave everything else in the cloud.

buildSteps.title: Choose and prepare sites
buildSteps.detail: Select locations with power, cooling capacity, physical security and a short, fast path to the devices — a telephone exchange, cell tower base, factory floor or retail back room.

buildSteps.title: Specify the hardware
buildSteps.detail: Pick CPUs, GPUs or neural accelerators, memory and storage to fit the workload in an enclosure rated for heat, dust and vibration.

buildSteps.title: Build the software image
buildSteps.detail: Assembly an operating system image with the container runtime, orchestrator agent and security stack, using read-only root and paired partitions so a failed update can roll back.

buildSteps.title: Install and connect
buildSteps.detail: Rack the node, connect power and network, and configure either fibre backhaul or a 5G link with local traffic breakout.

buildSteps.title: Provision remotely
buildSteps.detail: Enrol each node with a hardware-backed identity so it can fetch its configuration and workload images without anyone visiting the site.

buildSteps.title: Deploy workloads in stages
buildSteps.detail: Roll applications out to a small pilot site first, watch latency, error rates and resource use, then widen the rollout.

buildSteps.title: Operate the fleet
buildSteps.detail: Monitor from a central control plane, push model and software updates, and replace failed units — the hard part is doing this across thousands of unattended sites.

prerequisites.tech: Low-power, cheap multicore and accelerator chips
prerequisites.why: edge economics only work if the compute is small, quiet and inexpensive to replace.
packaging workloads makes them portable between cloud and many kinds of edge node.
fibre is widespread, but 5G with edge breakout is still being deployed and not yet ubiquitous.

prerequisites.tech: Remote fleet management and zero-touch provisioning
prerequisites.why: tooling exists but is immature for many thousands of heterogeneous, physically scattered nodes.
quantised models and accelerator runtimes let useful inference run on modest hardware.

pathway.milestone: content and function running in hundreds of distributed points of presence
pathway.unlocks: faster web and media delivery, and simple request-handling close to users.

pathway.milestone: telecom operators offering edge compute inside their access networks
pathway.unlocks: single-digit-millisecond latency for industrial control, cloud gaming and AR.

pathway.milestone: standardised management across mixed cloud and carrier edge sites
pathway.unlocks: one place to deploy and update workloads anywhere, without rewriting them.

pathway.milestone: a continuum of compute spanning device, edge and cloud with shared identity and data handling
pathway.unlocks: autonomous vehicles, real-time robotics and privacy-preserving local AI at scale.
